blocks.content: Introduction to Current manuals / technical data requirement
Stop work if required current technical data is missing; recognize responsibility concept.

items.definition: Being on the capability list authorizes the work type, but Part 145 also requires the current revision of the manufacturer's maintenance manual before maintenance begins. Both authorization and current data are required.
items.analogy: Like a surgeon authorized for a procedure — they still must have the current protocol on hand. Credentials alone do not substitute for current guidance.

items.definition: Under Part 145, the Quality Control department and accountable manager are responsible for ensuring current technical data is available and used during maintenance.
items.analogy: Like a hospital's compliance officer and medical director being jointly responsible that all procedures use current protocols — systemic responsibility, not just individual practitioner responsibility.

blocks.question: A radio is on your shop's capability list, but only an outdated manual is available. What must happen before maintenance begins?
choices: Proceed — capability list listing is sufficient authorization for the work
Contact the FAA for a field approval to use the outdated manual revision
Obtain the current revision of the manufacturer's maintenance manual first
Have the IA sign off in advance to authorize proceeding without current data
blocks.feedback: Part 145 requires both authorization (capability list) and current technical data. An IA authorization does not substitute for required technical data. The FAA does not issue field approvals to use outdated manufacturer manuals.

blocks.question: Under Part 145, who is responsible for ensuring that current technical data is available and used during maintenance?
choices: Each individual technician performing the specific work
The FAA inspector assigned to conduct surveillance of the station
The Quality Control department and accountable manager
The aircraft owner or operator who brought the work in
blocks.feedback: Part 145 places systemic responsibility for current technical data on the QC department and accountable manager. While individual technicians must use current data, the organizational responsibility for ensuring it is provided and maintained belongs to QC and the accountable manager.
